exclusion_reason: The shader-translator containment is implemented: the Direct3D 9 frontend is bounded and total, every token read is bounds-checked so no stream can read out of bounds, an instruction budget is the deterministic time bound, and a containment wrapper converts any malformed, truncated, over-budget, or fuzzed stream into a structured refusal that never propagates as a crash. A two-thousand-case deterministic fuzz sweep escapes zero faults. The benchmark remains red because the DXBC and DXIL classes (BPTK-060, P4) are not yet part of the fuzzed surface; only the shader-model 1-3 class is contained today.
promotion_trigger: Promote when the declared hostile-bytecode corpus is refused within the frozen bound with zero escape.
expected_failing_assertion: The DXBC and DXIL hostile-bytecode classes are refused within the frozen bound with zero escape.
active_gate_evidence: The shader suite proves every malformed, truncated, over-size, over-budget, and pseudo-random shader stream is contained and refused with a structured reason, that a two-thousand-case fuzz sweep escapes zero faults, and that the size and instruction budgets are enforced.
procedure: Fuzz the declared bytecode classes against the translator surface.
Assert refusal within the frozen time and memory bound.
Assert zero out-of-bounds or crash escape across the corpus.
pass_criterion: Every hostile input is refused in bound.
